title: Why New Orleans music endures; memories it brings back
summary: He calls the music versatile and culturally important, and says playing it stimulates old memories.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Why do you think this New Orleans music endures? I mean, you've played all kinds of music now, swing music, and probably almost a little bebop. I mean, I've heard, you know, all that sort of thing. Why do you think this music that came out of New Orleans is still, you know, really attracts attention and people still like to play it?

First, from a cultural standpoint, I think from the making of a nation, from the beginning, and say the childhood of a nation, this thing began. And they contribute so much to this culture. And I think that going back into this, at this time, to be a part of that is an honor. And so many of the old-time musicians have devoted and dedicated their life, and devoted much time, and most of their lives, and receiving a very little pay to put this on the map, see that this gets started. And so since that, I'm glad that I could take a part in it in some way, and contribute a little bit to what I can. It's so much they have given to this country.
But what is it about the music, George? What is it about this New Orleans music that still seems to affect people?

The New Orleans music is versatile. It can go from the mood, to the moody music, for as far as the blues, to the exciting part. And most of the exciting part is so exciting until it just goes in your toes, and your head will come out of your toes. And so it's just different, different from all the music.

Different from any music in the world. Mm-hmm. And I've heard some people say, hey, the music that you hear down there, you can't hear it nowhere else in the world. And I heard that when I was a little bit of a boy. My father told me that.
And so work came out to be true. I found this to be true, rather, in later years.
Well, I hope I see New Orleans this year, George. Yeah.
But while I'm saying that, I like to say this, it also filled me when I'm playing this music. It brings back so many memories.
And it seems like the stimulator, it stimulates my mind and my body also.

By doing certain things, certain things people play that remind me of a certain person that did the same thing down there at that time. I'm so glad that I have this alertness to pick up on this, and I say, to bring back these memories.
Yeah. Are you surprised sometimes when those little phrases pop out of your horn and you go, oh my goodness, I remember when somebody did that in 1921, you know?
Yes. Yeah. It's all in there.
